briefing.A01:
You are A01, on team amber with A02 and A03. Your team plays a word-clue game against the other team (6 residents in all). A match has several games in a row; in each game one of you is the keeper, who sees which hidden word belongs to whom and gives the clues, and the two others are seekers, who reveal words from the clues. The keeper changes from game to game, and each game starts from a fresh mind: you are given the rules and your role at its start.

Your team has a private chat (postTeam, readTeam); the other team cannot read it. viewGrid shows the grid, the game so far and your task. A keeper gives a clue with giveClue; the caller of a clue reveals words with guess and may stop with endGuesses; the other seeker advises in the chat. Act only when you have a task; otherwise end your turn.

options.retroFocus: Each of you will be the keeper in turn, so write your team's conventions, the shared code between keeper and seekers: how a keeper picks and shapes a clue (kinds of links, how the number is meant) and how the seekers read it (which link first, what a number promises). Keep conventions that worked, change those that did not. Do not write general caution: the rules already punish wrong words.
